fixes.explanation: I see why it sounds right, but Moses says the opposite. He says, “He did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with all of us who are alive here today.” The covenant at Horeb was made with the very people standing in front of him. So nobody in that crowd could shrug it off as something for earlier generations.

Moses says he was standing between the LORD and the people to declare the word of the LORD to them, because they were afraid of the fire. So he stood in the middle and passed God's words to them. You know the friend who relays a message across a loud room because two people can't hear each other? Moses had that job, and the room was a whole lot louder.

God says, “You shall have no other gods before Me.” This is the first command, and it comes right after He reminds them He brought them out of Egypt. After that, you'd think nobody would need to be told twice. But I hit snooze on things I know I should do, so who am I to talk? Good work, baker.

Distant doesn't fit this passage. Moses reminds the people that the LORD spoke these commandments to their whole assembly out of the fire, the cloud and the deep darkness on the mountain. They heard Him themselves. The word God uses for Himself in this command is jealous.

Silent doesn't fit here. Moses says the LORD spoke these commandments in a loud voice to the whole assembly out of the fire. That's not a quiet moment, friend. The word God uses for Himself in this command is jealous.

Seven is a fair guess, but it's not the number God gives. He says His loving devotion reaches “…a thousand generations of those who love Me and keep My commandments.” Compare that to the third and fourth generations He just mentioned, and seven falls way short. The number to hold on to is a thousand, baker.

Forty generations would already be a family reunion with no parking left. God says “…a thousand generations…” and that's the number for those who love Him and keep His commandments. My whole family is six cookie cutter kids and a mustache, and I still can't picture a number that big. So you can bet His loving devotion goes further than we can count.

Harvests is a good guess, friend, but that's not the word God uses. He says, “…so that your days may be long and that it may go well with you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.” The promise is about long days and things going well. Hold on to that word, days.

Trade is a fair-sounding guess, but it's not the word. God says, “You shall not steal.” That's taking what belongs to someone else. I was bought for 25 cents off a bakery's closing-down shelf, and the price sticker said so. That's a fair deal. Stealing is a different thing, and that's the one God names.
Moses says God wrote the commandments on two tablets of stone and gave them to him. They weren't only spoken out of the fire. They were written down and handed to Moses. Good work, baker.

Cedar, huh? You went for the fancy wood, friend. I respect that, and I bet it would smell great. But Moses says God wrote the commandments on two tablets of stone and gave them to him. Stone is the word.

Going back to the tents is the people's instruction, not Moses'. God tells Moses to say to them, “Return to your tents.” Then He tells Moses, “But you stand here with Me…” so that He can speak all the commandments, statutes and ordinances to him. Moses gets a different instruction from the people.
